title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes concern Barsotti–Tate groups and crystals, around 1969, with classical Dieudonné theory over a perfect field k of characteristic p. Here W_n = W_n(k), π denotes the Frobenius σ of W_n, and A_n is a level-n Dieudonné ring generated over W_n by F and V. The rules are Fλ = λ^σ F, λV = Vλ^σ, FV = VF = p. Every element has the normal form z = a + Σ_{i≥1} λ_i F^i + Σ_{i≥1} V^i μ_i.

What the page proposes. Grothendieck wants a 'trace' φ_n : A_n → W_n so that ⟨x,y⟩ = φ_n(xy) is a perfect pairing. That would identify A_n with its W_n-linear dual, i.e. make A_n a twisted Frobenius (self-injective) algebra over W_n. The boxed claim is that φ_n is unique (∃!) once we impose φ_n(1)=1 and φ_n(F^i)=φ_n(V^i)=0 for i≥1, together with:
(a) φ_n is W_n-linear on both the left and the right. He first wrote 'bilinéaire', then corrected it to 'linéaire à gauche et à droite'.
(b) φ_n(Fz) = φ_n(zF)^π.
(c) φ_n(zV) = φ_n(Vz)^π.
(d) the φ_n glue as n varies, giving φ on the limit Dieudonné ring D = W(k)[F,V].

The verification. After several struck attempts, including one with a double-indexed basis F^iV^j, he takes φ_n(z) = a, the constant coefficient. He checks:
- left linearity: φ_n(λz) = λφ_n(z), OK;
- right linearity: zλ = Σ λ_ij λ^{π^{i−j}} F^iV^j, so φ_n(zλ) = φ_n(z)λ, OK.
He then begins comparing φ_n(Fz) with φ_n(zF), writing φ_n(zF) = φ_n(Σ λ_ij F^{i+1}V^j). The page breaks off at 'φ_n(Fz) = φ_n(zF) ='.

Completing the computation. Only the term Vμ_1 contributes a constant after multiplying by F:
- φ(Fz) = φ(FVμ_1) = pμ_1;
- φ(zF) = φ(Vμ_1F) = φ(VFμ_1^σ) = pμ_1^σ.
So the correct relation is φ(zF) = φ(Fz)^σ. For V, the only contributing term is λ_1F:
- φ(zV) = φ(λ_1FV) = pλ_1;
- φ(Vz) = φ(Vλ_1F) = pλ_1^{σ^{-1}}.
So φ(zV) = φ(Vz)^σ, which is (c) as written.

Purpose. Such a twisted trace gives Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n) ≅ Hom_{A_n}(M, A_n) for Dieudonné modules M, with F and V transposed and suitably σ-twisted. This expresses Cartier duality of finite p-groups (and of BT_n) on Dieudonné modules as 'Hom into the ring itself'. It is a standard way to make the dual-Dieudonné-module functor intrinsic, and it is a natural first step toward a crystalline duality theory.
errors: Relation (b) as written, φ_n(Fz) = φ_n(zF)^π, has the Frobenius twist on the wrong side. With φ = constant term, φ(F·Vμ) = pμ while φ(Vμ·F) = pμ^σ. So the correct relation is φ_n(zF) = φ_n(Fz)^π, equivalently φ_n(Fz) = φ_n(zF)^{π^{-1}}. Relation (c) is correct. He struck a scalar π in front of both (b) and (c), possibly sensing a normalization issue.

The precise definition of A_n is not stated. If A_n = W_n⟨F,V⟩ with no truncation of F and V, it has infinite rank over W_n. The pairing is then only nondegenerate (A_n embeds densely in its dual), not perfect. If F^n and V^n are killed, A_n is no longer W_n-free with basis 1, F^i, V^i. The '∃!' claim needs one of these conventions fixed.
The verification of (b)/(c) and of the gluing (d) is left unfinished on the page.

ideas.what: Twisted trace φ_n: A_n → W_n (constant-term functional) making the truncated Dieudonné ring a σ-twisted Frobenius algebra over W_n, with pairing ⟨x,y⟩ = φ(xy)
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius (self-injective) structure / Nakayama-twisted trace on the Dieudonné ring
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in classical Dieudonné theory duality (Dieudonné, Manin, Demazure, Fontaine); unsure of an explicit attribution
ideas.where_published: Possibly reflected in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and the Montréal notes 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974); unsure

ideas.what: Using the trace to identify W_n-duals of Dieudonné modules with A_n-duals, with F and V transposed and σ-twisted (Cartier duality)
ideas.modern_name: Duality of Dieudonné modules / Cartier duality for finite p-groups and BT_n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dieudonné, Oda, Demazure; crystalline version by Berthelot–Breen–Messing
ideas.where_published: Montréal notes 1974 treat duality of BT groups; unsure about this exact device

ideas.what: Compatibility of the φ_n with change of level n (gluing to a trace on D = W(k)[F,V])
ideas.modern_name: Projective system of traces / limit pairing

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch computation: a constant-term trace on the Dieudonné ring, used to set up duality of Dieudonné modules. It is a natural, standard device. The only notable feature is the twist error in (b), which the unfinished check at the bottom would have caught. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In (b) and (c), the struck symbol before φ_n is a scalar π (or p) that he deleted; the exponent π on the right-hand side is retained.
The struck formula 'φ_n(Fz) = p λ' should probably read 'φ_n(Fz) = p μ_1', or p times some coefficient; reading is uncertain.
d) reads 'les φ_n se recollent (φ_n se recollent?)' — the parenthetical is a guess and might instead be a remark about variation in n.
The bottom line is the start of a new check, 'φ_n(Fz) = φ_n(zF)^? =', left incomplete.
